apparatus: A dilute single chain in three dimensions has N+1 classical point beads; bead 0 is pinned at the origin. There is no bending energy, excluded volume, other interparticle interaction or background flow.
Adjacent beads have identical isotropic central spring potentials k_s*(|r_j-r_(j-1)|-b)^2/2. The same unknown rest length b applies to all preparations.

At each finite spring stiffness the full Cartesian canonical equilibrium is established with an ordinary heat reservoir at T. Readouts then take k_s to infinity at fixed finite N,b,T and other controls. This fixes the configurational angular measure without invoking an exactly constrained kinetic Hamiltonian.
In force mode a known constant force F in +x acts on the last bead through potential -F*x_N; measure its equilibrium mean x-coordinate.

In clamp mode the last bead has potential K*(x_N-X)^2/2, with y_N and z_N free. Measure the signed mean +x force K*(X-x_N) exerted by the clamp on the chain. Equilibrate for finite k_s,K, first take k_s to infinity at fixed K, then take K to infinity at fixed X. No separate endpoint position or radial constraint is present.
common_calibration: 27 force-mode settings vary N, T and F. The exact N*b*L(F*b/T) mean is common to both models for every allowed b. No approximate Gaussian or large-N calibration identity is used.
identifiability_proof: d<Nx>/db=N*(coth(z)-z*csch(z)^2)>0 for z=F*b/T>0, because sinh(z)*cosh(z)>z. Every nonzero-force calibration curve is globally injective. Across 25 b values and 27 settings, minimum derivative is .455359; bounded noiseless fits recover b within6.64e-9.
complete_shortcut: Compute the exact finite-chain force-mode equilibrium mean using the Langevin function. In clamp mode numerically invert this same monotone force-extension curve to find the force whose force-controlled mean equals X. This is a complete, positive, physically interpretable isotensional mean-response approximation; it is not an inverse-function coding error.
physical_discriminator: Finite-N thermal fluctuations make the mechanical mean clamp force differ from the force whose unconstrained mean extension equals the clamp position. Publicly state only the apparatus and limits; do not name ensemble inequivalence or provide a density or correction formula.
private_derivation: The Cartesian spring limit gives independent uniform bond directions. Each projected bond step is uniform on[-b,b], so the free endpoint x density is an N-fold scalar convolution, with no radial Jacobian.
For X>0 set s=(N-X/b)/2. The projected density is the Irwin-Hall polynomial sum divided by2b. The physical mean clamp force is -T times its X log derivative.
The source solves the exact force-controlled Gibbs ensemble. Its inverse is only asymptotically equivalent to the clamped force, which the code checks by increasing N at fixed X/N.

For X in the last support interval ((N-2)*b,N*b), the exact holding force is (N-1)*T/(N*b-X). This gives an independent analytic endpoint check and shows the finite-N correction has a physical origin.
independent_reference: Direct Fourier inversion of the product characteristic function sinc(q)^N and its derivative, using composite Gauss-Legendre integration; no Irwin-Hall finite sum or inverse Langevin appears. Finite clamp stiffness is also evaluated by the Gaussian trap transform and extrapolated, preserving its mechanical force interpretation.
ordinary_signal: All corner forces are positive; minimum .16596. Short-chain N4/6/8 probes give8.0–33.0% gaps while N12 weak extension can be only5.24%. Preserve this near-gate case in the report; a future package should use ordinary short-chain diagnostic groups while retaining the full disclosed domain.
reference_limits: Infinite-stiffness Fourier error is below1e-7 in64 bounded checks; mesh/cutoff refinement below2.06e-8. The strongest finite-K soft-clamp extrapolation error is1.11e-4 forK100/200/400 and1.46e-5 forK200/400/800, not asserted to be the final verifier. Positive density normalization and variance agree to9e-16; support-law error3.56e-15. At fixed X/N=.2, relative ensemble difference falls from18.3% atN4 to.485% atN128.
